title: Export a flythrough video | Verse Engine by Ctruh
description: Export a flythrough video in the Verse Engine by Ctruh docs: what it is, how to use it, and where it fits in your 3D workflow.

docs.article:
Export a flythrough video#

Every streamed scene can become a client-ready MP4 or WebM — recorded from the live engine, in the viewer's own browser, with nothing uploaded and no server render farm. Two ways to get one: a button in the playground, or exportVideo() in an embed.

You need: a scene that has a tour. Scenes compiled with auto-staging already do (the server writes a ~30 s loop into <id>.stage.json: an orbit for open-sky scenes, a walkthrough through the largest open rooms for interiors). A recorded tour (?tour=) works too, and in embeds a scene with no tour at all gets a synthesized orbit of its framing sphere.

From the playground#

  1. Open the share link. Once the scene is up, a Tour chip appears — and beside it, Export video.
  2. Click it and pick duration (defaults to the tour length), resolution (1080p / 720p / native) and go.
  3. The file downloads as <scene>-tour.mp4 (H.264, where the browser can mux MP4: Chrome/Edge 126+, Safari) or .webm (VP9 elsewhere). The chip is labelled with the container you will actually get.

During capture the engine pins render scale to 1 (no dynamic resolution), blocks on-demand parking, and runs the render target at the output resolution; everything restores afterwards, including on cancel.

For scripting and QA the same thing is one call in the page console:

Code
await window.__verseExportVideo({ duration: 10, fps: 30, height: 1080, format: "mp4", download: true });
// resolves the Blob; download:false keeps it in memory

From an embed#

The capture runs inside the engine iframe (that is where the canvas lives) and the finished bytes transfer to your page as a Blob, so your page decides: download, upload to your own storage, or preview inline.

Code
<div id="viewer"></div>
<button id="make-video">Export video</button> <button id="cancel" hidden>Cancel</button>
<progress id="bar" max="100" value="0" hidden></progress>
<script src="https://HOST/embed.js"></script>
<script>
  const viewer = Verse.embed(document.getElementById("viewer"), { scene: "docs-demo-718035483f84" });
  const bar = document.getElementById("bar"), cancel = document.getElementById("cancel");
  viewer.on("export-progress", (p) => (bar.value = p.percent));

  document.getElementById("make-video").onclick = async () => {
    bar.hidden = cancel.hidden = false;
    try {
      const r = await viewer.exportVideo({ duration: 10, fps: 30, height: 1080 });
      if (!r.cancelled) {
        // r.blob is yours. Download it…
        const a = Object.assign(document.createElement("a"), { href: URL.createObjectURL(r.blob), download: r.name });
        a.click();
        // …or upload it: fetch("/my/upload", { method: "POST", body: r.blob })
      }
    } catch (e) {
      console.warn("export failed:", e.message);   // "no scene loaded yet", "an export is already running"
    } finally {
      bar.hidden = cancel.hidden = true;
    }
  };
  cancel.onclick = () => viewer.cancelExport();     // the pending promise resolves { cancelled: true }
</script>

Options#

OptionDefaultMeaning
durationtour lengthseconds, clamped 1–600
fps30clamped 5–60
height1080output height in px; 0 = the canvas's native height
formatauto (MP4 where supported)"mp4" or "webm"
bitrate~10 Mbps at 1080p, scaled by areavideo bits per second

Resolves { blob, mimeType, name, width, height, frames, cancelled }. One export runs at a time; export-progress events fire per captured frame and an export-done { id, size, cancelled, error? } event summarises the run for analytics (the bytes ride the promise, not the event).

Without the SDK#

If you talk to the iframe yourself, three messages do the job: verse:export-video { id, duration?, fps?, height?, format?, bitrate? } down; verse:event { name: "export-progress", detail: { id, percent, frame, total } } up while capturing; finally verse:export-video-done { id, bytes (transferred ArrayBuffer), mime, name, width, height, frames, cancelled } — or { id, error } on refusal (busy, no scene, recording unsupported). verse:export-video-cancel { id } cancels.

Getting a better video#

  • Pick the camera path first. Record your own with the editor's ⏺ Record tour (&edit=1), publish it with POST /v1/tour, and open the scene through the resulting ?tour= link before exporting.
  • 1080p at 30 fps is the sweet spot for listings and review decks; height: 0 captures the panel's native resolution when you need 4K from a 4K display.
  • The export records exactly what the viewer renders, so quality knobs apply: see Tune quality knobs — ?scale=1 is pinned for you, ?ssr=1 and ?hdr=0 are worth setting explicitly for a video destined for SDR screens.
